usdRate.sourceName: European Central Bank euro reference rate (USD)
usdRate.note: USD 1.1172 per euro on 30 October 2026, i.e. EUR 0.8951 per US dollar; World Bank 2025 average 0.885.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: INSEE consumer price index for France, September 2026 (French indices are the ones used in Monaco, per IMSEE)
inflation_cpi.note: Monaco publishes no consumer price index of its own; IMSEE's 'Monaco en Chiffres' lists the INSEE French CPI among the main French indices used in the Principality. French CPI +3.1% year on year (final, published 15 October 2026).

inflation_projection.sourceName: European Central Bank 2% inflation target (Monaco uses the euro)
inflation_projection.note: Monaco uses the euro under an agreement with the EU, so the ECB's credible 2% medium-term target is used.

policy_rate.sourceName: European Central Bank key interest rates (deposit facility rate)
policy_rate.note: Monaco uses the euro; the ECB deposit facility rate has been 2.50% since 16 September 2026 (main refinancing 2.65%).

savings_account_rate.note: Monaco has no national statistics on bank deposit rates and banks there are mostly private banks; no official average savings rate for Monaco was found.

fdr_3m_rate.note: No official statistics on 3-month term deposit rates in Monaco were found.

fdr_1y_rate.note: No official statistics on 1-year term deposit rates in Monaco were found.

dps_rate.note: No recurring-deposit product or published rate was found for Monaco.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Monaco has no central bank or deposit-rate statistics of its own; banks follow French banking law but no published average rate for Monaco-based banks was found.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Monaco has no public debt, so the State sells no savings certificates or retail bonds (Government of Monaco, national budget strategy page: https://www.gouv.mc/en/policy-practice/ensuring-economic-policy-is-fit-for-the-challenges-ahead/defining-and-managing-the-national-budget-strategy).

tbill_91d_rate.note: Monaco has no public debt and issues no treasury bills (Government of Monaco, national budget strategy page).

tbond_5y_rate.note: Monaco has no public debt and issues no government bonds (Government of Monaco, national budget strategy page).

tbond_10y_rate.note: Monaco has no public debt and issues no government bonds (Government of Monaco, national budget strategy page).

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: Monaco public service portal: tax in Monaco
tax_bank_interest.note: Residents genuinely established in Monaco pay no personal income tax, so bank interest is untaxed; French nationals resident in Monaco remain taxable in France under the 1963 convention.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: Not applicable: Monaco has no public debt and issues no government savings certificates (gouv.mc national budget strategy page: https://www.gouv.mc/en/policy-practice/ensuring-economic-policy-is-fit-for-the-challenges-ahead/defining-and-managing-the-national-budget-strategy); residents other than French nationals pay no income tax in any case.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: French Deposit Guarantee and Resolution Fund (FGDR), which covers banks headquartered in Monaco
deposit_insurance_limit.note: EUR 100,000 per customer per bank; the FGDR covers banks whose head office is in the Principality of Monaco.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No source stating a legal cap or typical credit card rate for Monaco was found.

equity_return_low.sourceName: No local stock market; global equities in EUR; ECB deposit rate 2.5%
equity_return_low.note: Low case: global shares return only a little above euro deposits over the long run.

equity_return_base.sourceName: Global equity long-run return about 6-7% in EUR; ECB deposit rate 2.5% (no tax on interest for residents)
equity_return_base.note: Monaco has no stock exchange, so the base is a global index fund in euros, kept within about 3.5 points of the 2.5% euro safe rate.

equity_return_high.sourceName: Global equity long-run returns in EUR
equity_return_high.note: High case: strong global equity returns over the long run.

gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold roughly flat after the 2025-26 spike, with a stable euro.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); ECB 2% target
gold_return_base.note: Base case: gold rises about 4.5% a year in euros, a little above inflation.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in euros.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: ECB deposit facility rate 2.5% (Sep 2026); no tax on interest for non-French residents
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: euro rates fall back toward 1.5%.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: ECB deposit facility rate 2.5% (Sep 2026); no tax on interest
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: euro deposits and money funds earn about the ECB deposit rate, untaxed in Monaco.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: ECB deposit facility rate 2.5%; euro-area bond yields
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: euro rates stay higher and savers lock in longer euro-area government bonds.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: Insurers in Monaco are mostly French insurers approved by the Monaco government; no Monaco life claim settlement ratio is published.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover is sold in Monaco (mainly by insurers approved under French rules), but no published premium table per EUR 1,000 of cover by age was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Employees are covered by the CCSS health insurance fund; no official figure for the out-of-pocket cost of a major hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: No published table of private (top-up) health insurance premiums per EUR 100,000 of cover was found.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: INSEE CPI Sep 2026: health services +0.8%, health products -2.3% year on year; ECB 2% target
goal_inflation_health.note: Private medical costs in Monaco tend to rise faster than the 2% target, so 3% is used.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: ECB 2% target; private and international school fees
goal_inflation_education.note: No education price index exists for Monaco; private and international school fees usually rise faster than general prices, so 3.5% is used.

life_expectancy.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_expectancy.note: Men 84.8, women 88.8 (UN WPP estimate for the year 2026, dated mid-year); World Bank 2024 figure 86.5.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years computed from georank's expected age at death by current age (UN WPP 2026 estimate).

support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio 71.7 (2025); no UN WPP projection for 2040 or 2065 could be read (populationpyramid.net has no Monaco page).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Caisses Sociales de Monaco, CAR direct pension
retirement_age_default.note: Legal retirement age 65; a CAR pension can be taken from 60 without reduction once all work has stopped, and from 55 for mothers who raised three children; at least 10 years of activity are required.

retirement_age_government.note: Civil service pensions are governed by Law 1.049 of 1982 and Law 975 of 1975, but no current text stating the retirement age limit for State employees could be read.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: euro deposit rates fall back toward 1%.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: ECB deposit facility rate 2.5% (Sep 2026); no tax on interest for residents
retirement_return_base.note: Base case kept below the 2.5% euro safe rate, since Monaco has no government bills and banks pay less than the ECB rate on many deposits.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: ECB deposit facility rate 2.5%; euro-area bond yields
retirement_return_high.note: High case: savers hold longer euro-area government bonds at about 3%.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Euro safe rate 2.5%; global equity low case 3%
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares and rates both disappoint.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Euro safe rate 2.5%; global equity in EUR 6%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half euro fixed income and half global shares.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: Euro bonds 3.5%; global equity high case 8.5%
retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Monaco pays a means-tested monthly retirement allowance (AMR) to non-Monegasque residents aged 65+ and a national old-age allowance to low-income Monegasques aged 60+, but the 2026 amounts (set by ministerial decree) could not be found.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: Monaco public service portal: how to apply for a monthly retirement allowance (updated 11 November 2025)
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Monthly retirement allowance (AMR) for non-Monegasques aged over 65 (60 if unfit for work) with at least 5 years' continuous residence and household income below a yearly threshold; Monegasque nationals over 60 on a low income get the national old-age allowance from the Town Hall social services.

gratuity_rule.note: No statutory end-of-service gratuity per year of service was found; Monaco labour law provides dismissal indemnities, but the text could not be read to confirm other rules.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Caisses Sociales de Monaco, CAR direct pension; Monaco public service portal (tax)
public_pension_scheme.note: Mandatory points-based basic pension (CAR) for private-sector employees plus the supplementary CMRC scheme; monthly pension = points x annual point value (EUR 22.27 from 1 October 2026) / 12, revalued by ministerial order rather than automatic indexation; +1.5% per quarter deferred after 65 (max 30%). Residents other than French nationals pay no income tax on it.

savings_account.note: Rates are set by each bank; no published average for Monaco.

dps.note: No standard recurring-deposit product was identified.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: Monaco has no public debt and sells no savings certificates.

tbill_91d.note: Monaco issues no treasury bills (no public debt).

tbond_5y.note: Monaco issues no government bonds (no public debt); residents can buy euro-area government bonds.

tbond_10y.note: Monaco issues no government bonds (no public debt).

equity_fund.note: No local stock exchange; diversified euro and global funds are available through banks.

centralBank.name: European Central Bank (Monaco uses the euro)

insuranceRegulator.name: Government of Monaco, insurance approvals (Business Development Agency)
insuranceRegulator.note: Insurers need Monaco government approval to extend their French (ACPR) licence to the Principality.

pensionScheme.name: Caisses Sociales de Monaco, Caisse Autonome des Retraites (CAR)

oldAgeAllowance.name: Department of Social Welfare (DASO), monthly retirement allowance

publicHealthCover.name: Caisses Sociales de Monaco, Caisse de Compensation des Services Sociaux (CCSS)

depositInsurance.name: Fonds de Garantie des Dépôts et de Résolution (FGDR), covering banks headquartered in Monaco
